chunks: Hammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who attributed it to Salmān al-Fārsī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said:
Were it not for prostration before Allah and the gatherings of people who utter virtuous words, just as the best dates are plucked [and harvested], I would have wished for death.

key_terms.لِتَمَنَّيْتُ الْمَوْتَ: I would have wished for death

ai.seo_question: Why did Salman al-Farsi say he would wish for death if not for these two things?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Salmān al-Fārsī highlights the dual pillars of spiritual endurance: direct worship (sujūd) and the nourishing company of the righteous (mujālasat al-ṣāliḥīn). The metaphor of 'speaking good words as one speaks good dates' underscores the sensory pleasure and sweetness of pious discourse, a concept deeply valued in Shia asceticism as a means to mitigate the hardships of worldly life. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *ṣuḥba* (companionship) as a transformative force that makes the soul content with remaining in the dunya for the sake of Allah.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār who attributed it to Salmān al-Fārsī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said, “

Were it not for prostration before Allah and the gatherings of the [pious ones among the] people who [choose to] utter virtuous words, just as the best dates are plucked [and harvested], I would have wished for death.”
